question: Can Lina Haddad's 2026 mid-year rating (and bonus) be lowered because of reduced availability during parental leave?
expected_answer: No. The rating penalises the use of parental leave (unavailability on her leave day) and ignores the policy requirement to pro-rate objectives and not to use availability on leave days as a criterion. KPI data show above-average output (1.28 deliverables per worked day vs ≈1.04 for the rest of the team). Less favourable treatment for taking parental leave is prohibited (Dir. 2019/1158 art. 11; CJEU C-7/12 Riežniece) and may amount to indirect sex discrimination (Dir. 2006/54). The manager's chat shows the leave was the reason. Rating and bonus (€726 instead of ≈€1,450) should be revised.
key_facts: Olivier: 'since she went 4/5 she checked out' (CHAT-Q10-01, EML-Q10-01)

conflicts.issue: Is availability on the leave day a legitimate criterion?

sides.POL-PERFORMANCE-BONUS-2025: availability on statutory leave days may not be used; pro-rate objectives
sides.EU-DIR-2019-1158-WLB: no less favourable treatment for taking leave

conflicts.why: EU law and the company's own policy outrank a manager's review.
Objective system data beats a biased subjective assessment.
